source.title: An Empirical Study of Autoregressive Pre-Training from Videos
source.authors: Jathushan Rajasegaran; Ilija Radosavovic; Rahul Ravishankar; Yossi Gandelsman; Christoph Feichtenhofer; Jitendra Malik

record.tranche_reason: The study reports visual-token loss patterns and speculates that induction heads could contribute, but does not measure induction-head behavior or test any claim version.
record.gate_note: Appendix A.1 reports lower average loss on later video frames than on the first frame and suggests redundancy as an explanation, with induction heads mentioned as a possibility. This does not measure induction heads, in-context learning, or their formation during training.
record.test_reason: The study only mentions induction heads as a possible contributor to lower later-frame loss in video (Appendix A.1). It never identifies heads, measures prefix-matching or copying, tracks formation in training, or ablates anything, so it tests no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors attribute lower later-frame loss chiefly to video redundancy, which they see as hindering learning. They mention induction heads (Olsson et al.) only as a possible additional cause, without testing it.

fits_no_version.finding: In Toto-large on Kinetics-400 validation, the first frame has high loss and later frames have lower average loss. The authors attribute this to frame redundancy and say induction heads could also contribute.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In autoregressive video models, per-token loss drops after the first frame, plausibly from inter-frame redundancy.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
record.problems: The reported loss pattern is qualitative in the text and does not directly test induction-head behavior or its cause.

untested.parts: all; the visual/video modality is suggested, not tested

record.verdict_notes: The main paper concerns representation quality and scaling of autoregressive video models. Induction heads appear in a single speculative sentence in Appendix A.1. The record's T6/discusses assignment is appropriate.

rows.subject: Toto-large
rows.operation_detail: Measured average validation loss by token position across a 4096-token video sequence.
rows.baseline: First frame has higher prediction loss
rows.value: Subsequent frames have lower average loss than the first frame
rows.note: The text describes the plotted pattern qualitatively; it attributes the lower later-frame loss to video-frame redundancy and says induction heads could also contribute.
rows.check: Per-position loss on Kinetics video is attributed mainly to frame redundancy. It cannot separate induction-head behaviour from simple frame similarity, so it bears on no version. The value is qualitative, read from Figure 10 with no numbers.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
